newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania central bank mulls mark/dlr litas peg-agency.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania central bank mulls mark/dlr litas peg-agency.

text.p: The central bank of Lithuania is considering pegging litas currency to both the dollar and the German mark as part of reforming its strict currency regime, the Baltic News Service (BNS) quoted a bank official as saying.

The litas is currently pegged at four to one dollar under a currency board, which means the central bank has to keep the local currency in circulation matched to the amount of hard reserves in its vaults.

BNS quoted central bank policy department head Gitanas Nauseda as telling a meeting of industrialists that the bank was working on a plan under which the litas would fluctuate in line with a mark/dollar basket.

Nauseda, who was not available to confirm the report, was quoted as saying that the current exchange rate should be maintained, fluctuating only slightly in line with the fluctuations in the mark/dollar basket.
The new right-wing government has set as one of its main aims ending the currency peg, which it says has led to an overvalued currency that strangles exports.
Nauseda's statements are the first comments from anyone at the central bank on the exchange rate system it prefers.
But a bank spokeswoman said Nauseda's remarks did not mean anything had been definitely decided by the bank.
Under the currency board, the central bank has no powers to influence monetary policy and is left mainly to monitor the smooth functioning of the currency peg.

BNS quoted Nauseda as saying that there would be three stages to the new system -- ending the currency board in the first half of 1997 and then changing the legislation that currently sets the exchange rate.
BNS also quoted Nauseda as saying that in the third stage of the move to a new system, the litas would be gradually reoriented to a peg to the mark, pushing out the dollar.
BNS quoted Nauseda as saying that the mark had been chosen as the base for the peg as it was to be the core of the new European currency, the euro.
